About

I'm a computer science student at the University of Toronto. I like working on software that has to make sense outside a demo.

Recent projects have taken me from smart glasses to web agents and a research prototype about memory. Across them, I keep asking similar questions: What does the person using this actually need? What evidence supports the result? What happens when the input changes?

During an internship in Guangzhou, I led an AR exhibition-guide project and evaluated AI agent workflows. In a hackathon team, I built a campus question desk that shows its sources. Independent projects give me room to explore smaller problems in more depth.

I also volunteered in rural AI education in Xinshao, China. When the classroom had no computer for the slides I had prepared, I switched to a simple robot story to explain machine learning. That experience changed how I think about explaining technical ideas: the explanation has to fit the situation in front of you.
